entry.title: The following letter has been written by a group of mothers of students at…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

The following letter has been written by a group of mothers of students at Sharif University of Technology to one of our colleagues, and in fact to the entire body of colleagues at Sharif University of Technology. Its audience is, in reality, all professors and officials of Iranian universities.——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————-We are a group of mothers whose children have, in recent months, faced heavy disciplinary rulings and expulsion from university. We write this letter not out of confrontation, nor to disregard the rules, but from the position of mothers who are worried about the future, the fate, and the lost years of youth of their children, and we have turned to you with great hope. Our children may have made mistakes or committed violations under certain circumstances, and it is natural that the university has the right to react to violations; but is taking away the opportunity to continue education and destroying the future path of a young person the only possible response to a mistake? What pains us most of all is the severity and sometimes irreparability of the punishment that affects the future of these young people. Many of these students have strived for years to get into Sharif University, have completed a significant portion of their studies, and their families have placed all their hope and resources into their future. What is most painful for us is that some of these students, in addition to the disciplinary case at the university and the expulsion ruling, have also faced punishment from the judicial system (mostly one to three years of imprisonment); that is, for a single offense at the university, they have faced two punishments from two institutions—the university and the judicial system! We ask you, if possible, to hear the voice of these mothers and, to the extent of your ability, help in reviewing the expulsion rulings, converting heavy punishments into more proportionate rulings, and providing the possibility for these students to return to the path of education. Sometimes a second chance can save a young person's life. We do not expect you to disregard the law; we only ask that alongside the law, fairness, proportionality of punishment, the circumstances of each student, and the future of a human being also be considered. If you have the means to follow up on these concerns or convey them to university officials or officials of the Ministry of Science, we sincerely request that you do not leave us alone. We thank you in advance for the time you take to hear our voice. With respect and hope, a group of mothers of expelled students of Sharif University of Technology

entry.title: This is what has been done in the recent book by Ahmad (Shahram) Shariati, a…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

This is what has been done in the recent book by Ahmad (Shahram) Shariati, a faculty member in physics at Al-Zahra University, whose books I have been reading for fifty years. This book, of course, does not have a sympathetic tone and criticizes Shariati apart from his valuable pains in an era when tyranny and silence cast a shadow over everything. For this reason, it is written very precisely and is full of references to the texts of Shariati's books and fact-checking of his claims. It is a book that, whether the admirers of Ali Shariati want it or not, will establish its place in all future years as a credible and precise reference for evaluating Shariati's record, and of course, like any other writing, it will be subjected to criticism. However, if the reader wants to know the era of Shariati and his life from childhood to death, they can refer to the book "Shariati, a Muslim in Search of Nowhere Land" written by Ali Rahnema. Perhaps after reading this book, the reader can look at some of Shariati's mistakes with indulgence. If our academic colleagues also want to look at the beginning and end of his work at Mashhad University, his teaching method, and his professional work, Jalal Matini's article is a valuable reference. Postscript: This writing is about Shariati as a university teacher. Fairness requires that anyone who criticizes Shariati as a social activist also consider that he missed the opportunity that his contemporaries found to see the later years and revise their beliefs. This is Shariati's tragic fate, and it means that it is said that Shariati remained unfinished.

entry.title: The story of Ashraf Marwan, son-in-law of Gamal Abdel Nasser and Mossad's…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

The story of Ashraf Marwan, son-in-law of Gamal Abdel Nasser and Mossad's intelligence source, is a complex example of this hidden war; where intelligence, trust, deception, and misanalysis were intertwined. But more important than the existence of a human agent is the lesson that can be learned from this case, and that is how the closest individuals can endorse a misanalysis of the situation under the guise of patriotic strategy and become part of the cycle of miscalculation. Therefore, if today within a country some create an atmosphere where decision-makers think that any tactical restraint or thought of agreement is a sign of weakness, or that any costly action is necessarily a sign of authority, in practice—even if their intentions are good—they may reproduce the same miscalculation that the enemy has invested years in creating. No wise commander spends all of a country's national capabilities in battle. No professional chess player sacrifices his queen merely to show boldness. Power is not in consuming tools; it is in preserving and using them at the right time. From this perspective, defending the country is not just defending borders; it is also defending strategic reason, even if they set up a faction or group or the rent of television and the country's platforms is in their name. Just as infiltration into a military center can threaten security, the infiltration of a wrong logic into the decision-making process can lead the country toward choices that the enemy did not even expect in its most optimistic scenarios. For this reason, a clear line must be drawn between resistance and extremism. Resistance is the art of increasing the enemy's cost with minimal national cost. Extremism is the readiness to pay any cost without calculating the cost-benefit ratio. The former creates deterrence; the latter may erode that very deterrence. A country that considers these two as one not only weakens the concept of resistance but also unintentionally exposes one of its most important defensive lines, namely the health of strategic calculations, to threat.

entry.title: Consequences of geopolitical stubbornness. On August 2, 1990, the Iraqi army,…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

Consequences of geopolitical stubbornness. On August 2, 1990, the Iraqi army, which at that time was called the fourth army in the world with 56 divisions and 700 fighter jets, invaded Kuwait in a lightning attack and declared it its nineteenth province. The international community, despite scattered objections from some countries like Jordan, Yemen, and the Palestine Liberation Organization, took a position against Saddam with a decisive majority. Just a few days after the invasion, the Security Council imposed the heaviest economic sanctions in history up to that time against Iraq with Resolution 661. Then the Security Council, through Resolution 678, gave Iraq until January 15, 1991, to withdraw unconditionally from Kuwait. In this interval, numerous peace plans and many mediations were offered to Iraq by the Soviet Union, France, Arab countries, and the UN Secretary-General; probably about 27 times. But Saddam, in "geopolitical stubbornness," made the withdrawal from Kuwait conditional on: Israel's withdrawal from occupied Palestinian territories and the liberation of holy Jerusalem. Saddam thought his capable army could inflict heavy casualties on American forces and that American public opinion would not tolerate a long, attritional war like Vietnam. He also estimated that the international and Arab coalition would fall apart with the start of the war. During the 90-day period of autumn 1990, all peace plans and mediations were rejected one after another by Saddam. The belief in the war becoming attritional, inflicting heavy casualties on America and defeating its public opinion, and the incorrect prediction about the collapse of the international coalition were completely false propositions on which Saddam's strategy of resistance was based. With the rejection of the last peace proposals, in January 1991, the operation called Desert Storm began. After a 39-day air war, during which Iraq's power grid, refineries, bridges, command centers, and communication routes were destroyed or rendered unusable, in a 100-hour ground battle, the defensive lines of the Iraqi army were worn down, and this army, with tens of thousands of casualties and the destruction of equipment, was forced to leave Kuwait. The heavy bombing of the Basra highway turned it into the "Highway of Death." Finally, Saddam's commanders at the Safwan tent, accepting the heavy ceasefire conditions of the coalition and America, surrendered with humiliating terms: -Destruction of missile and chemical weapons; -Acceptance of unconditional entry of UN and IAEA inspectors anywhere in Iraq; -And revision of borders in favor of Kuwait. Terms that were later consolidated in Resolution 687 (April 1991). #یدالله_کریمی_پور #karimipour_k

entry.title: On Monday morning, our university's technology center was bombed and completely…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

On Monday morning, our university's technology center was bombed and completely destroyed by Israel. No one hoped to be able to hold their virtual class session again, and we all thought our education would be closed until the end of this semester, and all students would lose an academic semester, especially when for each student losing a semester means falling behind a future they had planned and worked for years. But immediately, the company operating Skyroom in Iran made its service free for the university, and those involved in the university (the vice-chancellor and educational management and technology engineers) worked until the last hours of the night to create virtual classrooms for each professor, sent the addresses to all professors, informed thousands of students of the new addresses, sent new usernames and passwords in prepared lists to everyone, and presumably dozens of other tasks hidden from non-specialists. Virtual classes started again, and instead of a semester, only one day was interrupted. This was not a simple event, but a great and proud achievement that shows Iran is not just the Islamic Republic government, but a very worthy, respectable, and honorable ecosystem born of the creativity, knowledge, and efficiency of a wide range of specialists and patriots with various political thoughts and beliefs. Such an ecosystem must be defended with all our might against foreigners, ill-wishers, and the naive. Years ago, a European politician asked a mathematician, "Do these abstract things you do even help defend the nation?" and received the answer, "No, they don't help defend, but they make our nation worthy of defense." Our nation, too, is worthy of defense because of its abundance of intellectual, artistic, and industrial assets. Let us hope that the government also appreciates this ecosystem and compensates for its past mistakes so that all of us together—both those who stayed in Iran and that vast host of writers, artists, literati, and scientists who were forced to leave their homeland but have their hearts tied to their birthplace—can strive for the development of a prosperous and free Iran.

Greetings and respect to each and every dear representative of the units of the Iranian University Faculty Union. I, Alireza Aghaei, a member of the central council of the Iranian University Faculty Union, in protest against the election of the First Vice President as the head of the union! which took place tonight, January 4, 2026, resign from membership in the central council. It is my honor that in the previous term of the council, I received the first vote and in the current term, the second vote of the elected members of the twelve-member central council from you, the representatives of the union units in universities across the country, and I have been and am grateful for your trust. Nevertheless, while apologizing profusely to you, dear representatives of the union units, I consider the presence of the First Vice President in the position of head of the faculty union as a clear example of conflict of interest and an insult to the union, and I do not deem my membership in this council permissible. With renewed respect 🌹 Alireza Aghaei

Source: @vahidkarimipour

The intellectuals of Iran's Age of Awakening and the leftist intellectuals. What Beyzai says in this short clip is that during the reign of Reza Shah, these mausoleums were built: the tombs of Hafez, Saadi, Ferdowsi, Khayyam, Attar, and Baba Taher. Let's imagine Iran for a moment without these mausoleums to realize the importance of this work. All these deeds were accomplished through the efforts of the intellectuals of that era. In contrast, the leftist intellectuals also opposed Iran's literary luminaries such as Ferdowsi, solely because they were promoted by the Shah's regime.
